BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Seller's draft is the counterparty's position and has been reviewed critically against our playbook. Nothing in it has been accepted. No fallback positions have been authorised by Amelia Frost in respect of this draft.

---

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not, from our side. Almost every limitation provision has been drafted at or below our *unauthorised* fallback, several structural provisions would collapse the fundamental/title, fraud and specific-indemnity regimes into the general cap, and the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the key completion conditions (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title) are unresolved. Notably, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update – in several places it concedes exactly the gaps we need to press on.

Material departures are set out below in rough order of significance.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position. 20% is a conditional fallback usable **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at our fallback. We must not treat that as a meeting point. Respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the deal team wishes to consider 20% later, that requires Amelia Frost's written approval referencing this specific draft before anything is communicated to the Seller.

### 2.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each of which compounds the others:
- De minimis is 5x ours – on a business with ~AUD 12m revenue, a large number of genuine claims would fall away.
- Basket is 5x ours.
- "Excess above the basket" (deductible) rather than "tipping" basket. This alone costs us AUD 250,000 on any successful claim portfolio.
Push back on all three. The deductible construct in particular is not a playbook position at all and should be rejected outright.

### 2.3 Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims.
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
**Analysis:** Again the Seller has opened at our fallback. Hold at 24 months. The commercial rationale remains: 24 months captures two full audit cycles and the first full year of post-completion trading, which is when latent warranty issues typically surface.

### 2.4 "All Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – Clause 13 (and 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Seller:** Any limitation applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims "of any nature".
**Playbook:** Keep Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** This is the most dangerous drafting in the package and is easy to miss because it is framed as "administrative". Its effect is that the 20% cap, AUD 250,000 deductible basket and 18-month period would apply by default to:
- Title and capacity warranties
- Tax and IP warranties (which the Seller then declares "settled" – see 2.12)
- Specific indemnities (including Ironquay)
- Payment obligations and covenants (e.g. the Riverlark repayment, leakage, restrictive covenants)
- Potentially fraud (see 2.6)
We must reverse the default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; all other categories have their own expressly drafted regimes. Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 should each be confined to general Warranty Claims and expressly carve out fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct, title, capacity, specific indemnities and covenant/payment claims.

### 2.5 Fundamental / Title claims
**Seller:** Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** Reject in full. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20% recovery if it transpires we did not acquire good title to 100% of the shares – that is the entire consideration at risk. Title and capacity warranties must sit in a separate Fundamental Warranty schedule with the playbook regime. This also interacts with 2.13 (title evidence).

### 2.6 Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct
**Seller:** No express carve-out anywhere in the Seller Update; limitations expressly apply to Claims "of any nature".
**Playbook:** Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
**Analysis:** The absence of a fraud carve-out combined with the "all Claims of any nature" language is unacceptable. Insert an express, overriding carve-out in Clause 12 and in each of 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5. This is a non-negotiable playbook position and no member of the deal team has authority to trade it.

### 2.7 Disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Reject [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Require that only matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter** in the numbered specific disclosures qualify the Warranties. Public-register disclosure should be rejected or, at most, confined to a short list of named ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches dated within a specified window. Note also [1.4] – the blanket "no admission" paragraph is standard but we should ensure it cannot be used to argue that a disclosure was not "fair" because the Seller disclaimed its significance.

### 2.8 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This clause, read with 2.7, would effectively eliminate the warranty package – anything in the data room is deemed "discoverable" and therefore unclaimable. The extension to advisers and to constructive ("discoverable") knowledge is well outside market norms for an NSW SPA. Delete. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it belongs on the Seller's side (warranties qualified by the actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry), not as a bar on Buyer recovery.

### 2.9 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3 (Disclosure Letter [2])
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3 of the Bluefen contract) are satisfied, before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Disclosure Letter candidly admits that **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions** are in the data room. A "consent on delivery" test would be met by a conditional or qualified consent letter that leaves the 11.3 conditions outstanding. Require:
- Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under clause 11.2 **plus** documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition is satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen).
- Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer right to participate in communications and a long-stop date.
- Buyer-only waiver right.

### 2.10 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7 (Disclosure Letter [3])
**Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion".
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control trigger at clause 8.1. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room. A post-completion release leaves us owning a company in default under its facility with security still registered on PPSR. Require:
- Payout letter from Riverlark dated within an agreed window before Completion.
- Repayment directly from Completion funds per the funds flow (debt-free/cash-free mechanics).
- Executed deeds of release and PPSR discharge forms delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark/its solicitors to release on receipt of funds.
Any deviation from this requires Amelia Frost's prior approval. Do not accept the Seller's formulation.

### 2.11 Employee bonuses – Funds flow (Disclosure Letter [5])
**Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The bonuses are conditional on Completion – they crystallise as a liability of the Company (which we will own) at the moment we buy it. "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds them. The Disclosure Letter also concedes it does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. Require either:
- A specific Transaction Bonus line in the funds flow (gross amount + employer super + payroll tax + any other on-costs), paid by the Seller or deducted from the price; or
- Treatment as Debt / Transaction Expenses in the completion accounts with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing.

### 2.12 Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion and, via the "all Claims" default in 2.4, to subject them to the 20% / 18-month / deductible basket regime. Respond that Tax and IP remain open and will be addressed as separate categories with their own schedules. We should not at this stage assert unlimited liability – simply hold the position that they are not settled and are not within the general regime.

### 2.13 Title evidence – DD-012 (Disclosure Letter [10])
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter itself concedes DD-012 merely "identifies the source relied on" and does not state we have verified it. Before Completion we need, at minimum: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the shares; copies of share certificates; board/shareholder resolutions of Harbourglass Ventures approving the sale; constitution and any shareholders' agreement confirming no pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions; and a Seller warranty that the register is complete and accurate. This also reinforces why the Fundamental Warranty regime (2.5) must be preserved.

### 2.14 Ironquay IP indemnity – Clause 11.1 (Disclosure Letter [4])
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Disclosure Letter correctly notes this is not bank-verified non-payment, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The risk is not merely the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own IP it is using and may be exposed to infringement or licence-back claims. Require:
- Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (preserving the clause 7.3 cure path).
- Indemnity broadened to cover all Losses arising from any failure of SOW3 (or other Ironquay) IP to vest in the Company, including third-party claims, costs of re-procurement and remediation, not merely the fee itself.
- Indemnity to sit outside the general cap/basket/time limits.
Do not assert in correspondence that the AUD 180,000 is definitively owed or definitively paid – the record is open either way.

### 2.15 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Disclosure Letter [6])
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. The Disclosure Letter is appropriately careful – access, scope and notification status are unknown. We should mirror that discipline: do not characterise it as a notifiable data breach, and do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation either. Require:
- Covenant to preserve all relevant logs and correspondence.
- Covenant to complete the investigation (including any OAIC/notifiable data breach assessment) and provide written updates and the final report before Completion.
- Specific indemnity (or at least a specific warranty outside general disclosure) for Losses arising from the incident, triggered only if and to the extent loss materialises.
- Confirmation that the matter is not treated as "disclosed" against the data protection warranties by virtue of general disclosure.
No price adjustment is proposed at this stage.

### 2.16 Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011 (Disclosure Letter [8])
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so neither characterisation is proven. Request copies of the renewal terms, termination rights and accrual treatment in the Accounts. Reserve position on completion accounts treatment pending that information; do not concede "ordinary course" and do not demand a deduction yet.

### 2.17 Lesser items
- **Office lease (DD-007, [7]):** Notification obligation only on the Seller's reading. Request the lease, confirm whether notification is pre- or post-Completion and whether any landlord response/consent right follows. Add as a Seller pre-Completion covenant if notification is required before Completion.
- **Mossvale (DD-009, [9]):** Assignment restriction; Seller says no consent needed on a share sale. Review the actual clause for change-of-control wording. If none, accept with a specific warranty that no consent is required.
- **Disclosure Letter [11] (Reservation):** Unobjectionable and in fact helpful – it confirms no conclusion or approval is implied.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Hold 25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% needs Amelia Frost written authority – none given. |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | DM 25k; basket 250k; excess-only | **DM 5k; basket 50k; first-dollar.** Reject deductible structure. |
| 3 | Time limit (12.3) | 18 months | **Hold 24 months.** 18 needs Amelia Frost approval – none given. |
| 4 | "All Claims" default (13 / 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature | **Reverse default.** Limitations only on general Warranty Claims; separate regimes for Title/Tax/IP/indemnities/covenants. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Reject.** 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/DM/knowledge. |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out | Absent | **Insert overriding carve-out**; non-negotiable. |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, [1.1]–[1.2]) | Whole data room + public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only.** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket bar incl. advisers / "discoverable" | **Delete.** Any knowledge qualifier goes on Seller side, named persons + reasonable enquiry. |
| 9 | Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP:** unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion. |
| 10 | Riverlark (2 / 7) | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.** Deviation needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | **Specific line item incl. on-costs, or Seller-funded**; confirm super/payroll tax. |
| 12 | Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | **Not settled – OPEN.** Separate categories. |
| 13 | Title (DD-012) | Share register sufficient | **Independent evidence** (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority docs). |
| 14 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 fee only | **Broaden indemnity to IP vesting/Losses**; preserve 7.3 cure; procure confirmatory assignment. |
| 15 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, report pre-Completion; specific indemnity.** No breach assumed either way. |
| 16 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Request terms and accrual treatment; reserve position.** No auto Debt / no deduction yet. |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | **Review clauses; confirm by specific warranty/covenant.** |

**Process points:**
1. Do not communicate any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) to the Seller without Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying this draft.
2. The Disclosure Letter's own admissions in [2], [3], [4], [5], [6] and [10] should be quoted back to the Seller in our mark-up – they demonstrate the gaps the Seller Update glosses over.
3. Request an updated data room index and the underlying documents for Sandbar, the lease and Mossvale before the next turn.

If helpful, I can prepare the rider language for the fraud carve-out, the Fundamental Warranty schedule and the reversed Clause 13 default for insertion into our mark-up.

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20% recovery if it transpires we did not acquire good title to 100% of the shares – that is the entire consideration at risk. Title and capacity warranties must sit in a separate Fundamental Warranty schedule with the playbook regime. This also interacts with 2.13 (title evidence).

### 2.6 Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct
**Seller:** No express carve-out anywhere in the Seller Update; limitations expressly apply to Claims "of any nature".
**Playbook:** Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
**Analysis:** The absence of a fraud carve-out combined with the "all Claims of any nature" language is unacceptable. Insert an express, overriding carve-out in Clause 12 and in each of 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5. This is a non-negotiable playbook position and no member of the deal team has authority to trade it.

### 2.7 Disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Reject [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Require that only matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter** in the numbered specific disclosures qualify the Warranties. Public-register disclosure should be rejected or, at most, confined to a short list of named ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches dated within a specified window. Note also [1.4] – the blanket "no admission" paragraph is standard but we should ensure it cannot be used to argue that a disclosure was not "fair" because the Seller disclaimed its significance.

### 2.8 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This clause, read with 2.7, would effectively eliminate the warranty package – anything in the data room is deemed "discoverable" and therefore unclaimable. The extension to advisers and to constructive ("discoverable") knowledge is well outside market norms for an NSW SPA. Delete. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it belongs on the Seller's side (warranties qualified by the actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry), not as a bar on Buyer recovery.

### 2.9 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3 (Disclosure Letter [2])
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3 of the Bluefen contract) are satisfied, before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Disclosure Letter candidly admits that **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions** are in the data room. A "consent on delivery" test would be met by a conditional or qualified consent letter that leaves the 11.3 conditions outstanding. Require:
- Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under clause 11.2 **plus** documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition is satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen).
- Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer right to participate in communications and a long-stop date.
- Buyer-only waiver right.

### 2.10 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7 (Disclosure Letter [3])
**Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion".
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control trigger at clause 8.1. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room. A post-completion release leaves us owning a company in default under its facility with security still registered on PPSR. Require:
- Payout letter from Riverlark dated within an agreed window before Completion.
- Repayment directly from Completion funds per the funds flow (debt-free/cash-free mechanics).
- Executed deeds of release and PPSR discharge forms delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark/its solicitors to release on receipt of funds.
Any deviation from this requires Amelia Frost's prior approval. Do not accept the Seller's formulation.

### 2.11 Employee bonuses – Funds flow (Disclosure Letter [5])
**Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The bonuses are conditional on Completion – they crystallise as a liability of the Company (which we will own) at the moment we buy it. "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds them. The Disclosure Letter also concedes it does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. Require either:
- A specific Transaction Bonus line in the funds flow (gross amount + employer super + payroll tax + any other on-costs), paid by the Seller or deducted from the price; or
- Treatment as Debt / Transaction Expenses in the completion accounts with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing.

### 2.12 Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion and, via the "all Claims" default in 2.4, to subject them to the 20% / 18-month / deductible basket regime. Respond that Tax and IP remain open and will be addressed as separate categories with their own schedules. We should not at this stage assert unlimited liability – simply hold the position that they are not settled and are not within the general regime.

### 2.13 Title evidence – DD-012 (Disclosure Letter [10])
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter itself concedes DD-012 merely "identifies the source relied on" and does not state we have verified it. Before Completion we need, at minimum: current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the shares; copies of share certificates; board/shareholder resolutions of Harbourglass Ventures approving the sale; constitution and any shareholders' agreement confirming no pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions; and a Seller warranty that the register is complete and accurate. This also reinforces why the Fundamental Warranty regime (2.5) must be preserved.

### 2.14 Ironquay IP indemnity – Clause 11.1 (Disclosure Letter [4])
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Disclosure Letter correctly notes this is not bank-verified non-payment, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The risk is not merely the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own IP it is using and may be exposed to infringement or licence-back claims. Require:
- Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (preserving the clause 7.3 cure path).
- Indemnity broadened to cover all Losses arising from any failure of SOW3 (or other Ironquay) IP to vest in the Company, including third-party claims, costs of re-procurement and remediation, not merely the fee itself.
- Indemnity to sit outside the general cap/basket/time limits.
Do not assert in correspondence that the AUD 180,000 is definitively owed or definitively paid – the record is open either way.

### 2.15 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Disclosure Letter [6])
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. The Disclosure Letter is appropriately careful – access, scope and notification status are unknown. We should mirror that discipline: do not characterise it as a notifiable data breach, and do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation either. Require:
- Covenant to preserve all relevant logs and correspondence.
- Covenant to complete the investigation (including any OAIC/notifiable data breach assessment) and provide written updates and the final report before Completion.
- Specific indemnity (or at least a specific warranty outside general disclosure) for Losses arising from the incident, triggered only if and to the extent loss materialises.
- Confirmation that the matter is not treated as "disclosed" against the data protection warranties by virtue of general disclosure.
No price adjustment is proposed at this stage.

### 2.16 Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011 (Disclosure Letter [8])
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so neither characterisation is proven. Request copies of the renewal terms, termination rights and accrual treatment in the Accounts. Reserve position on completion accounts treatment pending that information; do not concede "ordinary course" and do not demand a deduction yet.
